title: Function design
body:
[[Structure chart]]
[[IPO Diagram]]
Always given

Designing one [[Function]] before writing it. The [[IPO Diagram]] for its box on the
[[Structure chart]] already answers most of it:

| IPO box | Becomes |
|---|---|
| Input | the [[Parameter]] list |
| Output | the return type, or a [[Call by reference\|reference parameter]] per extra result |
| Process | the body |

A function returns at most one value, so the moment a task has two outputs you are into
reference parameters. That is the one design decision this step actually forces.

The rest is a checklist:

- **One job.** If the name needs an "and" in it, it is two functions.
- **Name it after what it returns**, or after what it does: `is_prime`, `print_header`.
- **Prototype in the [[Header File]]**, definition below or in the `.cpp`.
- **Say what it assumes.** A comment stating what has to be true on entry and what is
  guaranteed on exit is the function's contract, and it is what makes it usable without
  reading the body. See [[Interface]].
- **Decide how you will test it** while you still remember what it was for: a [[Driver]] with
  normal, boundary, and bad inputs.

"One job" is cohesion and "small parameter list" is low coupling, which is the whole of
[[Coupling and Cohesion]] arriving four semesters early.
